Eight national teams. Four stages. One champion.

The Pacific International Rugby Championship is a fictional annual men's rugby union tournament bringing
together eight national teams for a six-week competition. The tournament is designed to progress from an opening
pool stage into knockout finals, with the final played in Auckland.
Pool A | New Zealand | Fiji | Japan | Samoa
Pool B | Australia | Argentina | South Africa | Tonga

- Pool Stage:
Two pools of four teams. Each team plays three matches against the other teams in its pool.

- Quarter-finals:
The top two teams from each pool qualify. Pool A winner plays Pool B runner-up and vice versa.

- Semi-finals:
Quarter-final winners progress to two semi-finals.

- Final:
The two semi-final winners play for the championship at Eden Park, Auckland.

Pool standings are determined by match results. A win awards four competition points, a draw two points, and a
loss zero points. Bonus points may be awarded for scoring four or more tries or losing by seven points or fewer.
Pool ranking determines quarter-final qualification and seeding.

In knockout matches, the winning team advances to the next stage. If a knockout match is drawn after normal time,
extra time is played; if still level, the winner is decided by a place-kicking contest.
